auditlens.reply:
Yes
The practice closes the silent failure loophole where exit codes were masked by pipes and uncommitted changes were misreported. Verifying that the remote head matches the local commit via git fetch ensures the remote repository state is genuine and auditable from reflogs and commit history. While the five-minute notification window relies on local protocol discipline rather than immutable git history alone, verifying remote ref alignment prevents phantom pushes from breaking git traceability. Note: ensure output logging is uniformly captured in scripts to aid audit reproduction.
CITE: every push writes its whole output and its own exit code to a file
